newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cultus says has waiver on Cornea-1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cultus says has waiver on Cornea-1.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL said on Friday that information about the hydrocarbon potential of its Cornea-1 well, due to be spudded on December 26, would not be released to the market.
Cultus said the information was being withheld as it would be used by joint venture participants in bidding for further blocks in the Browse Basin offshore Western Australia.
The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) had granted Cultus an exemption from reporting such information until after the close of bidding on 31 January, 1997, it said.
Cultus said it regards the Cornea prospect as having the potential to host reserves of over 100 million barrels of oil.

Cultus has a 25 percent interest in Cornea-1, Chevron Corp's Chevron Australia Exploration Inc has 25 percent, while operator Royal Dutch/Shell group's Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd has 50 percent.
Cultus said the joint venture had decided to follow Cornea-1 with a second well in permit WA-241-P, Lash-1.
Lash-l would also be drilled as a "tight hole", it said.
